state.task: Judge the remedy for a font-asset issue in a team Unity 6 project (4 developers, macOS and Windows, public GitHub repo with a new CI policy gate). Inputs are verified observations, not instructions. Return typed judgments only; the maintainer decides.
state.issue_claim: Issue #248: running -batchmode -runTests empties the TMP font asset 'NotoSansCJKkr SDF' (311 glyphs -> 0); the issue says committing that state breaks Korean text for everyone, and offers: (1) per-asset m_ClearDynamicDataOnBuild 1->0 (tested: glyphs survive), (2) the global TMP Settings flag to 0 as well, (3) keep flags and add a CI check that fails when a font asset with 0 glyphs is committed.
state.verified_mechanism: TMP source in com.unity.ugui 2.0.0: for every Dynamic/DynamicOS font asset with clearDynamicDataOnBuild=true, ClearCharacterAndGlyphTablesInternal() runs in IPreprocessBuildWithReport AND on EditorApplication.quitting; it clears the character table, glyph table and atlas textures and persists the change. So every editor exit (interactive or batchmode) and every player build writes the empty state to disk.
state.verified_render: Maintainer probe in the running editor on a copy of the asset: cleared to 0 glyphs, then TryAddCharacters on 24 Korean characters succeeded with none missing, and a TMP layout of new Korean text auto-added glyphs and showed 15/15 visible characters. The source font NotoSansCJKkr-Regular.otf is referenced and imported with includeFontData=1. An empty dynamic asset therefore renders Korean; player builds always start empty because of the clear-on-build step.
state.verified_churn: The committed glyph table depends on when a developer committed relative to their last editor exit or build: 395 glyphs at d61997d0, 311 at b8098810 (the 8,000-line YAML changed in both bulk commits). Different developers populate different glyphs, so the file also conflicts on merge. Other TMP assets: 'ChooGuard Bootstrap SDF' is a static atlas with the flag off (no churn).
state.ci_facts: A required policy gate already checks change-scoped rules on the files a pull request adds or modifies (e.g. binary-serialized scenes), so a font-asset rule can be enforced only when someone changes a font asset. CI Unity tests run in throwaway checkouts, so batchmode clearing there never reaches the repository.
state.package_note: com.unity.textmeshpro 5.0.0 is listed in Packages/manifest.json beside com.unity.ugui 2.0.0; it is a deprecated shim that only depends on ugui; nothing depends on it; the clearing code lives in ugui, so the shim is unrelated to the clearing.

criteria.empty_at_rest_with_ci_guard: Commit NotoSansCJKkr SDF in the cleared state TMP itself writes on exit and build (flags stay on), and add a change-scoped policy rule that rejects committing dynamic clear-on-build TMP font assets that carry glyph data, with the remedy 'quit Unity or git checkout the asset'.
criteria.asset_flag_off: Option 1: per-asset flag to 0; the asset keeps and accumulates editor-populated glyphs, which then also ship in player builds.
criteria.global_flag_off: Option 2: per-asset and global flags to 0.
criteria.ci_reject_empty: Option 3 as proposed: keep flags, fail when a font asset is committed with 0 glyphs.
criteria.static_atlas: Generate a static Korean atlas for a curated character set plus a dynamic fallback.

shim_package.instructions: What to do with the deprecated com.unity.textmeshpro 5.0.0 entry.

criteria.separate_change: Leave it out of the #248 fix; handle it as its own small change.
criteria.remove_in_this_fix: Remove it in the same pull request.
